description.narrative: The PDO is (i) to expand access to affordable broadband, (ii) to improve access to and adoption of selected digitally enabled public services, and (iii) to increase access to digital skills programs.

The development objective of the Burkina Faso - Digital Acceleration Project is to to expand access to affordable broadband, to improve access to and adoption of selected digitally enabled public services, and to increase access to digital skills programs. The project will consist of the following components: Component 1 (Expanding Digital Connectivity for Digital Inclusion) will help improve access to broadband connectivity by unlocking critical investments in the middle- and last-mile in areas controlled by the GoBF and by focusing on reforms that will improve affordability. Component 2 (Accelerating the Digital Transformation of Public Services for Inclusion and Universal Accessibility) will strengthen digital building blocks to increase access to public services through digitalization targeting the most vulnerable populations, including IDPs. Component 3 (Developing Digital Skills for the Knowledge Economy) will focus on boosting the supply and demand for digital skills and increasing the adoption of digital services provided by the public and private sector (see Table 1). The rapid inflow of IDPs has increased demand for digital infrastructure and services. Given the fragile environment in the Project area, the Borrower has prepared a security risk assessment and a security management plan, which will be continuously updated. Component 4 (Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation) will strengthen client's project implementation capacity. Component 5 (Contingent Emergency Response Component) will support the client to swiftly respond to crisis, if applicable. Given the national context of security concerns and the presidential directive to prioritize digitization, the Borrower's aim is to enhance the resilience of the digital back-end infrastructure (data hosting, national interoperability platform, digital security, etc.). Potential future investments can leverage the project's achievements and contribute to the long-term sustainability and resilience of the e-government's technical foundations.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries completing intermediate and advanced digital skills training under the project

comment.narrative:
Basic digital skills training aimed at national education students and teachers especially as part of emergency response through the learning continuity through digital project (sub-component 3.2.a). These activities may include, but not limited to, learning how to navigate a desktop computer, move and edit files, finding information on the internet, social media, and online safety.
Intermediate digital skills, include, but are not limited to, digital marketing, graphic design, or social media management. While advanced and specialized digital skills might include software development, cloud computing, Internet of Things, big data, artificil intelligence, and cybersecurity among other priority areas.
This indicator would also include the number of students attending the public high schools with STEM vocation which benefit from the project's support to provide research, innovation, and technology related services and courses to enable students address local challenges through digital.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries completing digital literacy training programs under the project

comment.narrative: Digital literacy training will support digital inclusion among the general population particularly the most vulnerable groups and contribute to increased adoption of public e-services as well as other innovative private platforms among the newly connected beneficiaries to broadband services under Component 1. In partnership with community-based organizations, this program will equip women, out-of-school youth, IDPs and PWDs with adequate skills to improve access to information that can improve beneficiaries productivity, employability and livelihood.

title.narrative: People benefiting from digitally enabled public services supported by the project

comment.narrative: Quantity of individuals who have accessed and benefited from public services that have been enhanced through digital. It aims to assess the reach and impact of initiatives that leverage digital platforms, tools, and processes to improve the delivery of public services. The indicator focuses on the number of people who have utilized digitally enhanced public services, such as Patient electronic medical records, Entrance competitions and professional examinations for the public administration or Administrative and legal proceedings. These services are designed to provide convenience, efficiency, and accessibility to citizens, enabling them to access and interact with public services in a more streamlined and user-friendly manner.

title.narrative: Newly built or upgraded digital infrastructure that is resilient to climate related shocks

comment.narrative: The newly built and upgraded broadband infrastructure under this project will be subject to quality standards that include compliance with the requirements for disaster response and for climate change mitigation (to be elaborated in bidding documents). These requirements will include, for example, the usage of weather-resistant materials, waterproof coverings, and underground infrastructure with climate-resilient design to withstand floods.
